claim: At d_model=256 (N=64, m2 fixed, seed 22, 6000 steps), final force R2 at the best-margin layer (layer 1) is 0.82857 against a control of 0.60495 (margin 0.224 ≥ 0.1). That is within 0.002 of the d_model=128 value (0.82669, layer 4) and within 0.005 of the d_model=64 value (0.8235, layer 1), so N=64 force at its best-margin layer does not rise with width. accel_step is also best at layer 1 with R2 0.92803 against a control of 0.74143, a headroom-normalised margin of 0.72. Distance (R2 0.991) and energy (R2 0.976) are decoded almost perfectly but fail the bar only because their d256 controls are 0.895 and 0.927. Against the paired d256 N=128 arm (run-20261016-042805-cfe4, force best layer 1), the gap can only be estimated from trajectory fields. The best-margin-layer estimate is about 0.03 (0.829 vs about 0.795). The max-over-layers estimate is about 0.07 (0.867 vs 0.795). Both are below the d64 gap of 0.143 and the d128 gap of 0.108.
confidence_note: This is one seed (22) on one dataset, and the pre-registered criterion is met. Three things limit confidence. (1) The three widths are compared at different layers: d64 at layer 1, d128 at layer 4, d256 at layer 1. (2) The trajectory's max-over-layers force R2 at step 6000 is 0.867, so some layer other than the best-margin layer 1 (one with a higher control) goes above the 0.86 'width still lifts force' cutoff. Read at the best layer by raw R2 instead of by margin, the result would fall on the expected-if-false side. A fixed-layer readout across d64/d128/d256 could flip the verdict. (3) The paired N=128 gap comes from trajectory fields, not probes_final, so it is an estimate and is not used as evidence here. The verdict would change if per-layer probes_final showed d256 force at some fixed layer at least 0.03 above the same layer at d128, or if a second seed (for example seed 23) moved by more than 0.03. Force was still rising slowly at step 6000 (+0.002 margin from 4500 to 6000).
